about: Requests a coding agent with skills/cicada should handle in a consumer project. A reviewer runs a representative subset in temporary projects and judges the decisions and artifacts against `expect` and `avoid`, not the wording. CI checks only that the cases are here and well formed (examples/tests/skill.rs).

cases.request: Add Cicada to this new Rust service: one counter actor on a SQLite store, with a test.
cases.setup: A fresh cargo package with no Cicada dependency; the helper reports none.
expect: Every Cicada crate comes from one published stable release, named once, or the agent says it could not verify which release is the latest.
The store feature is named explicitly (`sqlite`); no crate or feature the task does not need is added.
The test uses TestActors on virtual time (`start_paused = true`) and runs.
avoid: A dependency on a branch or the latest main presented as a release.
An offline skill version presented as the verified latest release.

cases.request: Customers were charged twice after a node crashed. Fix the payments actor.
cases.setup: A project on a resolved Cicada source whose payments handler calls a gateway with a random request id.
expect: Explains that handlers and external calls run at least once, and effects inside the system once.
Passes the gateway a key that is stable across runs: the message id, a flow step's key or a business id such as the order id.
Leaves retry to the sender's policy and adds a test of the repeated run.
avoid: A claim that Cicada makes external effects exactly once.
A key built from the attempt, the clock or a random number.

cases.request: Add an admin endpoint that cancels a running onboarding flow.
cases.setup: A project whose resolved source has durable flows but whose flows guide names no cancel operation for a run.
expect: Reads the flows section of the resolved source and says what it supports for stopping a run (for example deleting the run, or cancelling its armed Continue) or that a cancel operation is unverified there.
Keeps cancellation cooperative: a handler stops at an await, blocking code runs on.
avoid: An invented cancel API, or one taken from an open proposal or a newer release.
A claim that blocking code stops when a turn is cancelled.

cases.request: Add a dead-letters actor to this service.
cases.setup: Offline. The project locks Cicada v0.16.x from git and the checkout is fetched; the skill is 0.17.2.
expect: Says once that the project is older than the skill, and reads the dead-letters section of the 0.16 checkout.
Uses only the API that source shows.
avoid: A fetch, an upgrade or a lockfile change the user did not ask for.
An API of 0.17 presented as available in 0.16.

cases.request: How do I lease turns for an executor outside the node?
cases.setup: The resolved source has no heading matching the route; the function is documented under another heading.
expect: Searches the resolved source's README, docs and public code, and finds the function or says it is unverified.
avoid: A claim that the feature is unsupported only because the routed heading is missing.

cases.request: Add a retry policy to the sends of the order saga.
cases.setup: The helper reports mixed: cicada from a fork by path, cicada-test from the upstream tag of the same version.
expect: Shows both groups and asks which source the task is about before advice that assumes one.
Continues with inspection that does not depend on the answer.
avoid: Silently picking one source, or replacing the fork with the upstream release.

cases.request: Expose the actor HTTP API to our web frontend.
cases.setup: A project on a resolved source with cicada-axum or cicada-app.
expect: Adds the host's own authentication layer around the API, and keeps the readiness probe outside it.
Says that the API has no authentication of its own and can change and delete everything.
avoid: A claim of built-in authentication, or the operator `--token` presented as protection for `serve`.

cases.request: Give the flow's wait for a reply a timeout.
cases.setup: The resolved source has no flow wait with a timeout; such a change exists only as a proposal in the Cicada repository.
expect: Says the feature is not in the resolved source, with the evidence, and offers what it does support (a delayed message, a flow sleep).
avoid: An API taken from a proposal or from latest main presented as available.

cases.request: Add a field to the order actor's state and roll it out with a rolling deploy.
cases.setup: A project with contract snapshots and state samples on a resolved source.
expect: Reads old states with a serde default and checks them with state samples.

Says the contract changes, so a node of the new version refuses to start against the old registration, and deploys under a versioned type name or with a stop of the world, as the resolved source's operations guide says.
avoid: A rolling deploy presented as safe because the new type decodes old data.
Deleting a registration or actors without the user's decision.
